criteria.criterion: the seven components sum to the interaction, and a planted one comes back whole
criteria.detail: the seven components sum back to the interaction, worst relative gap 3.58e-16 over 40 tables. A leftover planted to vary only with gender comes back entirely in the gender component, worst gap 2.22e-16 over 5 draws. Degrees of freedom: education 2, age 2, gender 1, education x age 4, education x gender 2, age x gender 2, all three 4, summing to 17 = K - 1.
criteria.name: B106-11

criteria.criterion: whether the module's finer codes can answer the coarsening question
criteria.detail: the module also ships finer education and age codes. They cover 26 positions, on 1 industry code(s) (TOT) in 1 country (US). A table needs two positions carrying the same classes, so no table can be built from them and the finer granularity cannot be read here at all. Registered rather than attempted: D37's shape, a name in the listing with no record behind it.
criteria.name: B106-14

criteria.criterion: which part of the class grid carries the position-specific pay
criteria.detail: share of the interaction by class component, against the share each would take from a leftover with no structure, which is its own degrees of freedom over 17: education 21.0% vs 11.8% (1.78x); age 14.9% vs 11.8% (1.27x); gender 6.7% vs 5.9% (1.13x); education x gender 10.2% vs 11.8% (0.87x); education x age 20.3% vs 23.5% (0.86x); age x gender 9.3% vs 11.8% (0.79x); all three 17.7% vs 23.5% (0.75x). Both the shares and the floors sum to one, so a component above its floor forces another below it: what is read here is the ORDER, not seven independent readings. The order is that the single attributes are above and their interactions below, so the position-specific part of the ladder moves along one attribute at a time. Gender is the one part of the grid that is not coarsened, so its component cannot be composition inside a class shifting by position.
criteria.name: B106-12

criteria.criterion: whether each component repeats on its own
criteria.detail: adjacent-year correlation of each component on its own: education +0.9694 over 10,979; age +0.9598 over 10,979; gender +0.9578 over 10,979; education x gender +0.9512 over 10,979; education x age +0.9475 over 10,979; age x gender +0.9465 over 10,979; all three +0.9445 over 10,979. The competing reading puts every one of these at zero, since it puts the whole interaction at zero.
